cycles.name: Foundation Forge
focuses: Build foundational movement quality and neuromuscular efficiency across all major patterns.
Establish aerobic base and running consistency toward half marathon preparation.

cycles.name: Strength Engine
focuses: Build relative strength through progressive overload with new tools and increased training volume.
Extend Zone 2 run duration and consolidate walk-run protocol toward continuous running.

cycles.name: Metabolic Shift
focuses: Drive body recomposition through higher training density and elevated metabolic demand.
Develop single-leg and running-specific strength for race durability.

paragraphs: You went quiet for almost a month, and then you came back — lighter, honest about it, and you've shown up every session since. That's the whole game, Pegah. Cycle 3 is built on that: three focused days, nothing wasted, everything earns its place.

This is the cycle where the body composition work gets real. The proof is already there — your leg press doubled from 20 to 41kg in Cycle 2 — so now we make the sessions denser, put real load on your glutes with the hip thrust machine you like, and turn Day 2 into one clean job: run. Your mental focus this block is simple — protect the rhythm. Three days, every week, at whatever intensity that day allows.
By August 16 you'll be visibly stronger on every lift, running longer continuous stretches inside your zone, and your calves and glutes will be carrying you like a runner's should.
outcomes: Machine hip thrust loaded and progressing week over week
25–30 minutes of continuous running inside 139–152 bpm
First cycle of direct calf training complete — race-ready lower legs started
All three mandatory days hit, every week of the cycle
Every lift logged with honest RPE — including the soreness score

cycles.name: Race Ready
focuses: Peak running volume and muscular endurance for half marathon completion.
Maintain lean muscle and manage fatigue through smart load programming.

paragraphs: Your race is on the 19th of October. That's nine weeks away, and everything in this cycle points straight at it.

Day 4 is the long run, and it's the session that decides your race, so it isn't the optional one any more. It grows a little every week and it's supposed to feel easy the whole way. Walk whenever you need to. Walking is in the plan, it isn't you failing.

Your leg press went from 41 to 54 kilos last cycle and you never once had to grind a set to do it. Same idea here, just with real running on top. By the 20th of September you'll be covering 10km in one go and your legs will be handling it properly.
outcomes: Bulgarian split squat loaded and moving
Your first real hinge since the barbell stalled
Calves trained on kit your gym actually has
All four main days hit, every week
Week 1 long run logged with your average heart rate

cycles.name: Consolidate & Elevate
focuses: Integrate all physical qualities into a sustainable, high-performance lifestyle structure.
Post-race recovery, reflection, and transition into long-term athletic identity.

paragraphs: This is the one where the training stops being training.
The long runs get long, and then they get short again on purpose, and that's how you'll know it's close. Everything you build over the next five weeks gets pointed at one morning in October.
You won't be hoping you can finish it. You'll know.
Twenty-one kilometres. Go and take it.

days.completionMessage: Five exercises, under an hour, all of it useful. That's exactly how this day is meant to go.

good: Easy enough that you could hold a conversation the whole way through
Feel the legs waking up while the breathing stays comfortable
bad: Turning it into cardio. This is a warm-up, not a workout

good: Push the knees out against the band and lift to a straight line from knee to shoulder
Feel the glutes fire harder the more you push against the band
bad: Letting the band pull the knees inward

good: Hold the dowel down your spine and push your hips back toward the wall behind you
Feel the stretch build behind your thighs as the hips travel back
bad: Losing dowel contact at the head, upper back or hips. That means the back moved

good: Long arms, pull the band wide apart to chest height
Feel the muscles between the shoulder blades squeezing
bad: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears

exercises.name: Machine Leg Press
exercises.note: You finished last cycle on 54kg at a clean RPE 7 with room left in you. Start there and let the first set tell you whether it's ready to move again.

good: Feet hip-width on the platform, knees tracking over the toes through the whole range
Feel the quads and glutes sharing the load, driving through the whole foot rather than just the toes
bad: Locking the knees out hard at the top. Keep a slight bend and hold the tension

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: This is the hinge coming back. The barbell version stalled on you last time because of confidence, not strength, so we're using dumbbells where you can start light and own it. Go conservative on the first set and build from there.

good: Push your hips back toward the wall behind you and let the dumbbells slide down your thighs
Feel the stretch behind your thighs, never in your lower back
bad: Rounding your back to reach lower. Stop at the point your back stays flat

good: Drive the elbows down toward your back pockets and finish with the bar at your collarbone
Feel your lats doing the pulling rather than your arms
bad: Leaning back to drag the bar down with bodyweight

good: Push the handles straight away from your chest and control them all the way back
Feel your chest working through the whole push
bad: Letting the shoulders roll forward at the end of the press

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.note: Dumbbells instead of the cable, so your numbers finally mean the same thing at both your gyms.

good: Chest stays glued to the pad, row the dumbbells back toward your hips
Feel your back squeeze at the top before you lower under control
bad: Lifting your chest off the pad to heave a heavier dumbbell up

days.completionMessage: Steady minutes inside your zone are the ones that show up on race day. Nothing flashy about it, just banked.

good: Walk briskly until you feel warm, then start the drills
Feel the hips and ankles loosening before you ask them to run
bad: Skipping straight into the run cold

good: Long lunge, drop the back elbow inside the front foot, then rotate open to the ceiling
Feel the stretch through the back hip and the front of the thigh
bad: Rushing it. Hold each position long enough to actually feel it move

good: Band above the knees, sit into a quarter squat and step sideways with tension the whole time
Feel the outside of the hips switching on
bad: Letting the knees cave in or standing up tall between steps

good: Skip forward driving the opposite knee up and the arms through
Feel the ankles springing off the ground rather than the feet slapping down
bad: Reaching the foot out in front. Land it underneath you

exercises.name: Zone 2 Run
exercises.note: Your time climbs through the cycle: 35 minutes in week 1, then 40, 45 and 50, then back down to 35 in week 5. Talk test first, heart rate second.

good: Run at a pace where you could say a full sentence out loud without gasping
Feel the breathing stay rhythmic and controlled the whole way
bad: Racing yourself. If you can't talk, walk until you can

good: Feet up on the bench, curl your shoulders up off the floor toward your knees
Feel your abs doing the lifting rather than your neck
bad: Pulling on the back of your head with your hands

good: Knees bent, shoulders just off the floor, reach down and tap the side of your heel
Feel the side of your waist working on every reach
bad: Swinging side to side. Keep the reach slow and controlled

good: Legs straight and low, kick them up and down in small alternating beats
Feel your lower abs holding your back flat on the floor
bad: Letting your lower back arch up. Bend the knees a little if that happens

days.completionMessage: You didn't have to do this one. Your legs will feel looser tomorrow because you did.

exercises.name: Easy Walk or Walk-Jog
exercises.note: This one is genuinely easy. Last cycle you took your optional day up to 159bpm, which turns a recovery day into another hard day and steals from your long run.

good: Keep it easy enough that it feels almost too easy
Feel the legs flushing out rather than working
bad: Turning your recovery day into a third hard run

exercises.name: Long Run
exercises.note: Run this one continuously, at a pace where you could still hold a conversation. If you can't get a full sentence out, walk until you can and then start running again. That's the rule, not a failure. It grows every week: 6km, 7km, 8.5km, 10km, then an easier 6.5km in week 5. Week 1, run it by feel and send me your average heart rate.

good: Settle into a pace you could hold a conversation at and stay there
Feel your effort stay flat from start to finish rather than fading at the end
bad: Starting quicker than you can finish. The last kilometre should feel like the first

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.note: You sat on 5kg dumbbells all last cycle and it kept getting easier, so the back foot goes up on a bench now. That elevation IS the step up in difficulty, so drop the dumbbells lighter and let the first set find the weight.

Feel the front glute and quad pushing the floor away

exercises.name: Machine Hip Thrust
exercises.note: You went from 5kg to 10kg last cycle and it got easier as it went. Expect this one to move up faster than the rest.

good: Push the pad up through your heels until your hips are level with your knees
Feel the glutes squeeze hard and hold it for a full second at the top
bad: Finishing the rep by arching your lower back instead of squeezing your glutes

good: Back flat against the pad, curl your heels down and back under the seat
Feel the back of your thighs doing all the pulling
bad: Lifting your hips off the seat to get the last few reps

good: Press the handles straight up and control them back to ear height
Feel your shoulders carrying the load the whole way

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Single Leg Calf Raise
exercises.note: One dumbbell in one hand, one leg at a time, standing on a step. This is the fix for the standing calf machine your gym doesn't have.

good: Rise all the way up onto the ball of your foot, pause, then lower slowly to a full stretch
Feel the calf stretch fully at the bottom and squeeze hard at the top
bad: Bouncing out of the bottom. The slow lowering is the entire point

good: One heavy dumbbell in one hand, walk tall with it hanging straight down
Feel the opposite side of your trunk working to keep you upright
bad: Leaning away from the weight to make it easier

good: Knees bent, curl your hips up off the floor toward your ribs
Feel your lower abs doing the lifting
bad: Swinging your legs to build momentum

good: Opposite arm and leg reach away slowly, then come back under control
Feel your lower back staying pressed into the floor the whole time
bad: Letting the back arch as the leg goes out. Shorten the reach if it does

good: Sit back slightly with the feet down, rotate your hands from hip to hip
Feel the sides of your waist doing the turning

cards.title: Fifty-Four Kilos, And Climbing
cards.body:
Your leg press went 41 to 54 kilos last cycle and you never once ground out a set to get there. Every session landed right on target. That's the cleanest run of progress in your whole file.

Something else worth saying. Back in July I asked you to actually rate your soreness instead of leaving it on "none". You did, and it's been honest ever since. That's the reason I can read your weeks properly now.

You also came back from a month off and never disappeared again. Hold onto that when the long runs start getting long.

cards.title: More Core, Like You Asked
cards.body:
You asked for more and you've got three times as much. It's on Day 2 straight after your run and on Day 5, because those are the two days you never miss. All of it is simple stuff you can do tired.

One honest thing, because I'd rather say it now than have you wonder in five weeks. Crunches build the muscle underneath, they don't change what's over it. The shape of your middle comes from the running and from what you eat, and both of those are already moving in the right direction.

What this core work genuinely does is hold you together in the last few kilometres of your race, when form falls apart and everything starts to hurt. That's worth doing on its own.

So do it because you said you would, and let the running do the other job. You've never broken a promise to me yet.

cards.title: Day 4 Is The Whole Cycle
cards.body:
Everything else in this program exists to keep you healthy enough for Day 4. It's the session that decides your race, so it isn't the optional one any more.

Here's how it grows:

  • Week 1 · 6km
  • Week 2 · 7km
  • Week 3 · 8.5km
  • Week 4 · 10km
  • Week 5 · 6.5km, an easier week on purpose

Run it continuously. If you can't talk, walk until you can, then start running again. That's the rule for this session, and using it isn't failing. What matters is finishing the distance feeling like you had a bit more in you.

cards.title: Your Heart Rate Zone Was Wrong
cards.body:
I set 139 to 152 from your resting heart rate. You've been running at 154 to 159 and telling me you feel fine. You were right and my number was wrong. Your heart just runs a bit higher than the formula expects.

So let's do it properly. In week 1, run your long run purely by feel and send me the average heart rate afterwards. That number becomes your real zone for the rest of the cycle.

Until then the rule is the talk test. If you can say a full sentence out loud without gasping, you're in the right place. If you can't, walk until you can.

cards.title: The Calf Machine Thing Was On Me
cards.body:
You told me three times in your logs that your gym has no standing calf machine. I kept writing it in anyway. Sorry, that one's mine.

It's a dumbbell in one hand now, one leg at a time, standing on a step. You've got that at both your gyms.

It matters more than it looks. Your calves take more force per stride than anything else when you run, and the slow lowering into a full stretch is the whole point. Never bounce out of the bottom.

cards.title: Day 1 Is Short On Purpose
cards.body:
You've never finished a Day 1. Not because you were tired either, your Day 5 sessions run 90 minutes and you finish those every time. Day 1 is just about 50 minutes in your life, whatever day of the week it lands on.

So I stopped pretending otherwise. It's five exercises now and it's built to be done inside that. No finisher on the end, because your running is your conditioning this cycle.

If you're still tight for time, the row at the end is the one to drop. Everything in front of it earns its place.

cards.title: Two Gyms, Two Sets Of Numbers
cards.body:
You spotted this before I did. The cable machine at your other gym reads completely differently, so your row went 27, then 21, then 35, and none of it told me anything real.

That's why you're on dumbbell rows and dumbbell calf raises now. A 6kg dumbbell is 6kg everywhere.

On the machines you've still got, just say which gym you were at in the session note. Then I can actually read your numbers instead of guessing at them.

cards.title: Eating For The Longer Runs
cards.body:
Once your long run passes about an hour you're in new territory, and running it on empty is the quickest way to feel terrible and blame your fitness for it.

Start with these:

  • Something with carbs 1 to 2 hours before the long run. Toast and honey, a banana, porridge. Nothing new on the day.
  • From week 3, take something with you for anything over 70 minutes. A gel, dried fruit, a sports drink. Practise it now so race day isn't the first time you try it.
  • Protein and carbs within an hour after. A proper meal counts, it doesn't have to be a shake.

Tell me what you actually eat around your long run and we'll fix it from there. I'd rather sort out the real thing than hand you a plan you won't follow.

cards.title: Your Period-Week Menu
cards.body:
Same deal as last cycle, rewritten for these exercises so you never have to work it out while you're feeling rough.

  • Keep exactly as written: both runs, the easy day, and all the warm-up circuits. Light movement helps with cramping.
  • Cut to 2 sets and go visibly lighter: leg press, Romanian deadlift, Bulgarian split squat, hip thrust, lat pulldown, chest press, shoulder press and leg curl. Move the pattern, don't grind it.
  • Skip completely: the suitcase carry, and both core circuits. Anything with hard ab bracing waits for a normal week, and that's the one bit of this cycle I want you to skip without thinking twice about it.

This isn't about performance on those days. It's about not losing the week.
